description:
GEØ.IA brings together mathematics, data science and a young explorer's curiosity: Adriele Jardim (mathematics researcher), Geovanna Lim (founder of GEØ.AI and data scientist) and Ana Luiza dos Reis de Mello (elementary school student). We share one rule: every answer must be traceable to open data, and every limit must be stated. Built for NASA Space Apps 2026.

Meet the team: https://geoia-spaceapps.vercel.app/#team
summary:
GEØ.AI Planetary Intelligence is a web platform that answers one question: which documented places on Earthbest stand in for a given spot on the Moon or Mars, and why? The user picks a point on a 3D globe. In about a minute, the platform reads open NASA data live for that point: LRO LOLA and MGS MOLA laser altimetry, Chandrayaan-1 M³ and MRO CRISM spectroscopy, and, at the lunar south pole where permanent Artemis bases are planned, LOLA-derived illumination and permanent-shadow maps. It turns these data into screening-level mineral and terrain evidence and matches it to a curated catalog of 18 terrestrial analog sites documented in the literature. For each site it shows why it is an analog, where the analogy fails, and the exact data products and references used. Missing or unavailable data is reported as such, never as an absence. Analog sites are where astronauts train and where rovers and instruments are tested; choosing them with traceable, honest evidence
helps prepare Moon and Mars missions.
details:
WHAT IT DOES



GEØ.AI Planetary Intelligence links a point on the Moon or Mars to the places on Earth where it can be studied, rehearsed or tested.

1. Select: the user picks a point and a radius on a 3D Moon or Mars globe, by clicking the globe, typing coordinates, or choosing an example (Jezero, Gale, Meridiani, Mare Imbrium, Apollo 17).



2. Analyse: the backend runs a live analysis on NASA's public archives. Nothing is precomputed, and no synthetic value is ever shown as a measurement.



- Topography: real laser shots (LOLA RDR / MOLA PEDR) inside the circle: elevation, slope, roughness and coverage.

- Mineral screening: Moon, M³ band depths at 1 µm and 2 µm; Mars, the CRISM team's summary parameters (olivine, pyroxene, clays, carbonate, sulfate, ferric oxide, hydration, ice). Each indicator passes a statistical detection test and a physical floor calibrated on real negative controls.

- Earth analog sites: documented sites whose published geology explains what was detected, with coordinates, why each is an analog, its differences and limitations, and DOI-verified references. No similarity percentages.

- Lunar south pole: fraction of time sunlit, permanent shadow and Earth visibility from the LOLA/PGDA illumination models, the conditions a permanent base would face. The platform does not claim ice.

- Moon–Earth terrain comparison (experimental): lunar terrain (LOLA) and Earth sites (Copernicus DEM) profiled with the same method and scale, reported per exploration purpose (rover mobility, traverse planning, rugged-terrain operations).

- Sources: every value points to its product ID, observation date and URL. A downloadable PDF report is generated for each analysis.


3. Explain honestly: a missing measurement (no sunlight, permanent shadow, no coverage, a NASA service timeout) is reported as such, never as an absence of minerals. An inconclusive result produces no recommendation.


HOW IT WORKS

- Backend: Python 3.12 and FastAPI. It range-reads only the bytes it needs from NASA products (M³ and CRISM cubes, LOLA/MOLA through ODE GDS, polar illumination maps).

- Science modules compute the indicators, apply detection tests, controls and masks, and match the evidence to the analog catalog.

- Asynchronous jobs with per-step deadlines, so a slow NASA service affects only its own section. Results affected by a provider failure are not cached.

- Frontend: 3D globes and analysis panels, in English and Portuguese, with a local history of analyses.


VALIDATION


- 21 real-data scenarios, from Mars rover landing sites to lunar landing sites and the lunar south pole, with the expected outcome written before each run.

- Adversarial tests that try to push the system into wrong scientific conclusions.

- Thresholds calibrated on one set of real controls and validated on another, never used for calibration.

- 227 automated tests. Every release was re-checked in production against the previous one.


BENEFITS AND IMPACT

- For mission planners, field teams, students and the public: a transparent link between orbital data of a candidate site and real places on Earth for training, instrument testing and resource experiments.

- Honesty by design: every analog shows where it fails (different chemistry, no space weathering, atmosphere, vegetation, mining).

- Reproducible: each result lists the exact NASA products used, so anyone can verify it.


CREATIVITY


The same ruler is applied to both worlds: lunar and terrestrial terrain are measured with one method at one scale. The platform reports where an analogy breaks, not only where it holds, and treats missing data as unknown rather than absent. TOOLS Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, HTTPX, NumPy, ReportLab, SQLite, pytest, Docker; Render (backend hosting); Skip AI app builder (React) for the platform interface; Vercel (project site).


Source code: https://github.com/GeovannaLim/GEO.IA-PLANETARY-INTELLIGENCE-

NEXT STEPS

A positive plagioclase criterion for lunar highlands; Diviner thermal and polar ice data; more terrestrial sites with precise coordinates; discovering new candidate sites, not only matching documented ones.
